follow100Note: Of the $17.02 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, $0.16 belongs to non-controlling partners — $16.87 is Uber shareholders'. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Net income of $2,416M includes $22M attributable to non-controlling interests; $2,394M is attributable to Uber shareholders (the $1.17 EPS figure). Cost of revenue is shown excluding depreciation and amortization, exactly as Uber reports it.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: flattered by a $1.6B paper gain on investments

oneTimers: A ~$1.6B pre-tax benefit from revaluations of Uber's equity investments sits in other income — a paper gain, not cash from rides or deliveries. It also drove most of the quarter's $840M tax provision, which includes the deferred U.S. tax on those securities.
otherDetail: A $1,342M other-income gain — mostly a ~$1.6B pre-tax paper benefit from revaluing Uber's equity investments, partly offset by other losses — plus $172M of interest income, less $127M of interest expense and a $21M equity-method loss.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.note: Rides — the original Uber business. Revenue grew just 1%: business-model changes in how some trips are billed (insurance and driver costs) reshaped the top line even as bookings rose 22%.

segments.name: Delivery
segments.note: Food and grocery delivery — Uber Eats and couriers, growing far faster than rides.

segments.name: Freight
segments.note: Trucking logistics — matching shippers with carriers.

takeaways.text: Gross Bookings — everything riders and eaters spent on the platform — grew 24% to $58.0B, with trips up 18%. Revenue grew 12% to $14.2B; business-model changes in how some trips are billed held reported revenue growth about 8 points below bookings growth.
takeaways.title: Bookings still booming

takeaways.text: Operating income rose 30% to $1.9B and Adjusted EBITDA 33% to $2.8B. Free cash flow over the last twelve months passed $10B for the first time in Uber's history.
takeaways.title: Core profit up 30%

takeaways.text: GAAP net income of $2.4B includes a ~$1.6B pre-tax benefit from revaluing Uber's equity investments — and much of the quarter's unusually large $840M tax bill came with it. The cleaner read on the business is the $1.9B operating line.
takeaways.title: A paper gain did heavy lifting

verdict: Uber's bookings grew 24% to $58.0B and operating profit rose 30% to $1.9B — and the headline $2.4B profit also got a big lift from a $1.6B paper gain on its investment stakes.
